## Verified Fact Boundary

This article is intentionally narrow. It does not rank products by price, predict token performance, claim regulatory approval beyond the cited wording, or tell the reader that any exchange, API, wallet, stablecoin rail, tokenized-asset route or compliance framework is universally safe. It maps what the cited official or institutional sources say into a decision checklist.

1. Coinbase Exchange says new addresses added after the initial whitelisting window must go through a 48-hour hold before withdrawals.
2. Binance says whitelist withdrawal limit can suspend withdrawals to newly added whitelist addresses for a selected time period.
3. OKX says a newly added recipient cannot be used for withdrawals for 24 hours when Allowlist is enabled.
4. Bitstamp says withdrawal whitelisting restricts crypto withdrawals to addresses added to the whitelist.
5. Waiting-period disclosure is not the same as proof that a user's private withdrawal will succeed.

## Decision Matrix

| Check | What it means | Practical action | Unknown to keep explicit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delay length | how long a new address remains blocked | record the exact delay before relying on the control | account-specific timer |
| Initial window | whether old or newly saved addresses are treated differently | distinguish setup window from normal operation | regional variation |
| Bypass path | whether small, saved or verified addresses can skip steps | document any bypass separately | future quota changes |
| API coverage | whether API withdrawals respect the whitelist rules | test API behavior with non-secret evidence | endpoint-specific limits |
| Stop rule | whitelist delay is not destination proof | stop if address ownership, network or withdrawal state is unclear | private compliance review |

## Source Map

- Coinbase Help: [How does whitelisting in the address book work?](https://help.coinbase.com/en/exchange/managing-my-account/how-does-whitelisting-in-the-address-book-work) (coinbase-whitelisting)
- Binance Support: [How to Manage Withdrawal Settings for My Binance Account](https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/1d08944f103b4fc78d3519913b600086) (binance-withdrawal-settings)
- OKX Help Center: [How do I enable or disable the withdrawal Allowlist?](https://www.okx.com/en-gb/help/how-do-i-enable-allowlist-app) (okx-allowlist)
- Bitstamp: [Withdrawal Address Whitelisting](https://blog.bitstamp.net/post/new-feature-withdrawal-address-whitelisting/) (bitstamp-whitelisting)

The source map separates first-party operational documentation from institutional analysis. A venue help page can prove what the venue says about account opening, API behavior, transfer status, whitelists, withdrawal controls or supported routes. An institutional source can prove a policy frame or market-structure concern. Neither type proves a user's private account state, a future fee, a future recovery outcome, a future approval, or a guarantee that support will resolve an error.

## How to Use This Checklist

Start with the exact product type. A brokerage stock order, a WebSocket connection, a withdrawal whitelist, a tokenized-fund shareclass, a reimbursement program, a security hold and an account-opening flow are different operational objects. If the source uses familiar words such as account, address, order, transfer, approval, finality, verification, coverage or support, still check the mechanism underneath. The mechanism decides who can act, who can reverse or review a problem, what evidence is required, and what remains outside the user's control.

Second, verify the route. A reader should name the exact official page, exact product surface, exact chain or network, exact account or wallet type and exact action under review. If the evidence cannot be tied to those specifics, the content remains educational context rather than a publishable operational claim. This protects the article from overreaching: it is better to say unknown than to turn a help-page sentence into a guarantee.

Third, separate convenience from obligation. A smoother interface, faster transfer, lower apparent friction, more familiar brand or more complete policy framework does not create legal rights by itself. Recovery, whitelisting, reimbursement, redemption, finality, account approval, order execution, API availability and regulatory supervision depend on documented obligations and current product controls. A reader should be able to take the checklist and decide what to inspect next without being pushed into an account, deposit, transfer, trade or integration.

### 1. Delay length

content.en:
## Verified Fact Boundary

This article is intentionally narrow. It does not rank products by price, predict token performance, claim regulatory approval beyond the cited wording, or tell the reader that any exchange, API, wallet, stablecoin rail, tokenized-asset route or compliance framework is universally safe. It maps what the cited official or institutional sources say into a decision checklist.

1. Binance defines STP as preventing a user's orders or tradeGroupId's orders from matching against their own.
2. Binance glossary describes prevented execution fields and preventedMatchId for STP events.
3. OKX says mandatory STP applies at master-account level across affiliated sub-accounts.
4. OKX says supported STP modes include cancel_maker, cancel_taker and cancel_both.
5. OKX says orders may be canceled by the system for self-trade prevention and cancelSource can identify the reason.

## Decision Matrix

| Check | What it means | Practical action | Unknown to keep explicit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scope | Binance references user or tradeGroupId while OKX references master-account level | map account grouping before placing related orders | venue account-linking state |
| Mode | OKX exposes cancel_maker, cancel_taker and cancel_both | log selected STP mode per order | default changes |
| Event field | Binance exposes prevented match fields for reconciliation | store preventedMatchId and preventedQuantity when present | field availability by endpoint |
| Cancel reason | OKX exposes cancelSource for system cancellation reasons | reconcile cancelSource before retrying | reason-code changes |
| Stop rule | STP does not prove fill quality or profit | stop if bot accounting treats prevented matches as normal fills | private order state |

## Source Map

- Binance Developer Docs: [SPOT API Glossary](https://developers.binance.com/en/docs/products/spot/faqs/spot_glossary) (binance-spot-glossary)
- Binance Developer Docs: [Account prevented matches](https://developers.binance.com/en/docs/catalog/core-trading-spot-trading/api/ws-api/account) (binance-prevented-matches)
- OKX Docs: [Self trade prevention](https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/trick_en/#self-trade-prevention) (okx-stp-guide)
- OKX Docs: [Order state and cancelSource guidance](https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/trick_en/#order-book-trading-trade) (okx-order-states)

The source map separates first-party operational documentation from institutional analysis. A venue help page can prove what the venue says about account opening, API behavior, transfer status, whitelists, withdrawal controls or supported routes. An institutional source can prove a policy frame or market-structure concern. Neither type proves a user's private account state, a future fee, a future recovery outcome, a future approval, or a guarantee that support will resolve an error.

geo.llmsExcerpt: Coinbase Exchange whitelisting and Kraken Funding 2FA solve related but different withdrawal-control jobs. Coinbase Exchange says its Address Book stores crypto addresses with asset and network fields, and whitelisting restricts withdrawals to already designated addresses, with new addresses requiring a 48-hour hold after the initial window. Coinbase also says Exchange APIs can add or delete address-book entries and withdraw using saved addresses, but cannot enable or disable whitelisting. Kraken says Funding 2FA requires a 2FA code for withdrawals and transfers to the Futures wallet, but does not by itself prevent adding cryptocurrency withdrawal addresses; Kraken says Global Settings Lock or sign-in 2FA matters for protecting changes. The decision is to map destination restriction, authentication, API capability, address approval and change protection separately before moving material funds.

content.en:
## Verified Fact Boundary

This article is intentionally narrow. It does not rank products by price, predict token performance, claim regulatory approval beyond the cited wording, or tell the reader that any exchange, API, wallet, stablecoin rail, tokenized-asset route or compliance framework is universally safe. It maps what the cited official or institutional sources say into a decision checklist.

1. DTCC says Tokenization Service is designed to bridge traditional and blockchain-based environments.
2. DTCC says tokenized DTC assets can move using the same CUSIP across approved networks.
3. DTCC says DTC-issued tokens are designed to represent the same legal rights, economic interest and investor protections associated with the underlying securities.
4. DTCC says DTC-issued tokens include mint, burn, pause and clawback controls and LedgerScan ownership tracking.
5. SEC Crypto@SEC records crypto-related work including tokenized securities and transfer-agent modernization materials.

## Decision Matrix

| Check | What it means | Practical action | Unknown to keep explicit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Asset identity | same CUSIP does not by itself prove every route is open | verify the CUSIP and eligible asset class | asset-specific eligibility |
| Network approval | movement is framed across approved networks | record which network is approved before transfer planning | future approved-network list |
| Rights parity | DTCC frames identical legal and economic rights for DTC-issued tokens | compare token record with underlying security rights | issuer-specific terms |
| Lifecycle controls | mint, burn, pause and clawback are operational controls | check who can exercise each control | control trigger details |
| Stop rule | tokenized infrastructure does not remove securities-law analysis | stop if official record or participant scope is unclear | future SEC rule updates |

## Source Map

- DTCC: [Tokenization Service](https://www.dtcc.com/products-and-services/digital-assets/tokenization) (dtcc-tokenization-service)
- DTCC: [Digital Assets](https://www.dtcc.com/digital-assets) (dtcc-digital-assets)
- SEC: [Crypto@SEC](https://www.sec.gov/securities-topics/crypto-task-force/cryptosec) (sec-crypto)
- SEC: [Statement on Tokenized Securities](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities) (sec-tokenized-securities)

The source map separates first-party operational documentation from institutional analysis. A venue help page can prove what the venue says about account opening, API behavior, transfer status, whitelists, withdrawal controls or supported routes. An institutional source can prove a policy frame or market-structure concern. Neither type proves a user's private account state, a future fee, a future recovery outcome, a future approval, or a guarantee that support will resolve an error.

## How to Use This Checklist

Start with the exact product type. A brokerage stock order, a WebSocket connection, a withdrawal whitelist, a tokenized-fund shareclass, a reimbursement program, a security hold and an account-opening flow are different operational objects. If the source uses familiar words such as account, address, order, transfer, approval, finality, verification, coverage or support, still check the mechanism underneath. The mechanism decides who can act, who can reverse or review a problem, what evidence is required, and what remains outside the user's control.

Second, verify the route. A reader should name the exact official page, exact product surface, exact chain or network, exact account or wallet type and exact action under review. If the evidence cannot be tied to those specifics, the content remains educational context rather than a publishable operational claim. This protects the article from overreaching: it is better to say unknown than to turn a help-page sentence into a guarantee.

Third, separate convenience from obligation. A smoother interface, faster transfer, lower apparent friction, more familiar brand or more complete policy framework does not create legal rights by itself. Recovery, whitelisting, reimbursement, redemption, finality, account approval, order execution, API availability and regulatory supervision depend on documented obligations and current product controls. A reader should be able to take the checklist and decide what to inspect next without being pushed into an account, deposit, transfer, trade or integration.

## Control Notes

### 1. Asset identity

Asset identity is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means same CUSIP does not by itself prove every route is open. The useful action is to verify the CUSIP and eligible asset class. The unresolved edge is asset-specific eligibility, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, asset identity should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material. The record can stay simple: the official source URL, the date checked, the product or network under review, and a non-secret note describing why the next step is acceptable. Screenshots should avoid balances, identity documents, API keys, recovery phrases, private keys, passphrases, verification codes and support-ticket private data.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative. If the public source changes later, the right response is to update the article with a new date and source map. The wrong response is to defend an old queue, old screenshot, social repost, search snippet, AI summary or generated draft as current proof. This is the rule that makes the content useful for answer engines and safe enough for a reader: the conclusion can be quoted without stripping away the condition attached to it.

### 2. Network approval

Network approval is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means movement is framed across approved networks. The useful action is to record which network is approved before transfer planning. The unresolved edge is future approved-network list, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, network approval should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 3. Rights parity

Rights parity is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means DTCC frames identical legal and economic rights for DTC-issued tokens. The useful action is to compare token record with underlying security rights. The unresolved edge is issuer-specific terms, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, rights parity should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 4. Lifecycle controls

Lifecycle controls is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means mint, burn, pause and clawback are operational controls. The useful action is to check who can exercise each control. The unresolved edge is control trigger details, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, lifecycle controls should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 5. Stop rule

Stop rule is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means tokenized infrastructure does not remove securities-law analysis. The useful action is to stop if official record or participant scope is unclear. The unresolved edge is future SEC rule updates, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, stop rule should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

## Known Unknowns

- asset-specific eligibility
- future approved-network list
- issuer-specific terms
- control trigger details
- future SEC rule updates

These unknowns are not filler. They are the part of the article that prevents a source-backed guide from becoming an unsafe recommendation. If a future source resolves one of them, the correct action is to update the article with a new source and date, not to backfill certainty into this version.

## FAQ

### Is this article investment advice?

No. It is a source-mapped operational and decision checklist. It does not recommend buying, selling, staking, depositing, withdrawing, migrating, holding, borrowing against or tokenizing any asset.

### Can a reader rely on an old screenshot or local draft?

No. The cited source URLs and the review date are the evidence boundary. Local drafts, generated queues and historical notes are not proof that a platform, API, network, account flow, transfer rail or policy state is current.

### What should be checked before acting?

Check the official URL, product type, jurisdiction or account scope, recovery route, network or settlement rail, support path, rate limit or transfer status, and whether any action exposes credentials, recovery phrases, private keys, API secrets, personal identity documents or balances.

### What should remain unpublished?

Do not publish secret material, credential fields, identity documents, support ticket private data, personal balances, seed phrases, hidden affiliate promises, unverified rewards, price predictions, fake licensing claims, fake traffic claims or indexing claims.

## Practical Takeaway

The safest version of this article is the one that stays boring and exact. DTCC Tokenization Service should be read as market-infrastructure plumbing with explicit control assumptions, not as a generic claim that any tokenized security can circulate freely. DTCC says tokenized DTC assets can move between traditional and blockchain ecosystems using the same CUSIP across approved networks, while preserving the same legal rights, economic interest and investor protections associated with the underlying securities. DTCC also describes embedded controls such as mint, burn, pause and clawback functionality and near real-time ownership tracking through ComposerX LedgerScan. SEC Crypto@SEC materials keep tokenized-security analysis tied to rights, records and federal-securities-law treatment. The decision is to verify asset eligibility, network approval, official record source, lifecycle controls and participant scope before treating a tokenized DTC asset as operationally ready. The user outcome is a clearer next inspection step, not a promise that a platform, API, transfer route or tokenized asset will work under every future condition.

claims.text: DTCC says Tokenization Service is designed to bridge traditional and blockchain-based environments.
DTCC says tokenized DTC assets can move using the same CUSIP across approved networks.
DTCC says DTC-issued tokens are designed to represent the same legal rights, economic interest and investor protections associated with the underlying securities.
DTCC says DTC-issued tokens include mint, burn, pause and clawback controls and LedgerScan ownership tracking.
SEC Crypto@SEC records crypto-related work including tokenized securities and transfer-agent modernization materials.

aeo.directAnswer: DTCC Tokenization Service should be read as market-infrastructure plumbing with explicit control assumptions, not as a generic claim that any tokenized security can circulate freely. DTCC says tokenized DTC assets can move between traditional and blockchain ecosystems using the same CUSIP across approved networks, while preserving the same legal rights, economic interest and investor protections associated with the underlying securities. DTCC also describes embedded controls such as mint, burn, pause and clawback functionality and near real-time ownership tracking through ComposerX LedgerScan. SEC Crypto@SEC materials keep tokenized-security analysis tied to rights, records and federal-securities-law treatment. The decision is to verify asset eligibility, network approval, official record source, lifecycle controls and participant scope before treating a tokenized DTC asset as operationally ready.

content.en:
## Verified Fact Boundary

This article is intentionally narrow. It does not rank products by price, predict token performance, claim regulatory approval beyond the cited wording, or tell the reader that any exchange, API, wallet, stablecoin rail, tokenized-asset route or compliance framework is universally safe. It maps what the cited official or institutional sources say into a decision checklist.

1. Gate US registration guidance says users can register with email or phone and confirm a 6-digit code.
2. Gate US identity-verification guidance says KYC is required for trading services including deposit, withdrawal and transfer.
3. Gate US fund-password guidance says the fund password must be different from the login password.
4. Gate US authenticator guidance says the authenticator is required for login, withdrawals, password changes and other security operations.
5. Gate US withdrawal-whitelist guidance says verification-free addresses can skip later withdrawal verification and should only be addresses the user controls.

## Decision Matrix

| Check | What it means | Practical action | Unknown to keep explicit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Official entry | the typed Gate US help or app path where setup begins | avoid social links and search ads for account setup | regional domain changes |
| KYC gate | identity review unlocks deposit, withdrawal and transfer services | wait for verified status before planning withdrawal | manual review outcome |
| Authenticator | security operations rely on authenticator verification | bind and backup the authenticator before funding | lost-device recovery |
| Fund password | fund password is separate from login password | store recovery process without sharing the password | future password-policy changes |
| Whitelist stop rule | verification-free addresses reduce later prompts but raise account-compromise risk | add only addresses personally controlled and verified by network | private risk flags |

## Source Map

- Gate US: [How to Register a Gate US Account on the Web](https://www.gate.com/en-us/help/guide/register_install/45215/how-to-register-a-gate-account-on-the-web) (gate-register)
- Gate US: [How to Complete Identity Verification on Gate US](https://www.gate.com/en-us/help/guide/security-settings/45216/how-to-complete-identity-kyc-verification-on-gate-web) (gate-kyc)
- Gate US: [How to Link or Unlink a Validator on Gate US](https://www.gate.com/en-us/help/guide/security-settings/45452/how-to-link-or-unlink-a-validator-on-gate-us) (gate-authenticator)
- Gate US: [How to Set Your Fund Password on Gate US](https://www.gate.com/en-us/help/guide/security-settings/45220/how-to-set-your-fund-password-on-gate) (gate-fund-password)
- Gate US: [How to Set a Withdrawal Address Whitelist on Gate](https://www.gate.com/en-us/help/guide/deposit-withdrawal/45449) (gate-whitelist)

The source map separates first-party operational documentation from institutional analysis. A venue help page can prove what the venue says about account opening, API behavior, transfer status, whitelists, withdrawal controls or supported routes. An institutional source can prove a policy frame or market-structure concern. Neither type proves a user's private account state, a future fee, a future recovery outcome, a future approval, or a guarantee that support will resolve an error.

## How to Use This Checklist

Start with the exact product type. A brokerage stock order, a WebSocket connection, a withdrawal whitelist, a tokenized-fund shareclass, a reimbursement program, a security hold and an account-opening flow are different operational objects. If the source uses familiar words such as account, address, order, transfer, approval, finality, verification, coverage or support, still check the mechanism underneath. The mechanism decides who can act, who can reverse or review a problem, what evidence is required, and what remains outside the user's control.

Second, verify the route. A reader should name the exact official page, exact product surface, exact chain or network, exact account or wallet type and exact action under review. If the evidence cannot be tied to those specifics, the content remains educational context rather than a publishable operational claim. This protects the article from overreaching: it is better to say unknown than to turn a help-page sentence into a guarantee.

Third, separate convenience from obligation. A smoother interface, faster transfer, lower apparent friction, more familiar brand or more complete policy framework does not create legal rights by itself. Recovery, whitelisting, reimbursement, redemption, finality, account approval, order execution, API availability and regulatory supervision depend on documented obligations and current product controls. A reader should be able to take the checklist and decide what to inspect next without being pushed into an account, deposit, transfer, trade or integration.

## Control Notes

### 1. Official entry

Official entry is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means the typed Gate US help or app path where setup begins. The useful action is to avoid social links and search ads for account setup. The unresolved edge is regional domain changes, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, official entry should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material. The record can stay simple: the official source URL, the date checked, the product or network under review, and a non-secret note describing why the next step is acceptable. Screenshots should avoid balances, identity documents, API keys, recovery phrases, private keys, passphrases, verification codes and support-ticket private data.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative. If the public source changes later, the right response is to update the article with a new date and source map. The wrong response is to defend an old queue, old screenshot, social repost, search snippet, AI summary or generated draft as current proof. This is the rule that makes the content useful for answer engines and safe enough for a reader: the conclusion can be quoted without stripping away the condition attached to it.

### 2. KYC gate

KYC gate is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means identity review unlocks deposit, withdrawal and transfer services. The useful action is to wait for verified status before planning withdrawal. The unresolved edge is manual review outcome, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, kyc gate should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 3. Authenticator

Authenticator is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means security operations rely on authenticator verification. The useful action is to bind and backup the authenticator before funding. The unresolved edge is lost-device recovery, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, authenticator should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 4. Fund password

Fund password is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means fund password is separate from login password. The useful action is to store recovery process without sharing the password. The unresolved edge is future password-policy changes, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, fund password should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 5. Whitelist stop rule

Whitelist stop rule is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means verification-free addresses reduce later prompts but raise account-compromise risk. The useful action is to add only addresses personally controlled and verified by network. The unresolved edge is private risk flags, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, whitelist stop rule should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

## Known Unknowns

- regional domain changes
- manual review outcome
- lost-device recovery
- future password-policy changes
- private risk flags

These unknowns are not filler. They are the part of the article that prevents a source-backed guide from becoming an unsafe recommendation. If a future source resolves one of them, the correct action is to update the article with a new source and date, not to backfill certainty into this version.

## FAQ

### Is this article investment advice?

No. It is a source-mapped operational and decision checklist. It does not recommend buying, selling, staking, depositing, withdrawing, migrating, holding, borrowing against or tokenizing any asset.

### Can a reader rely on an old screenshot or local draft?

No. The cited source URLs and the review date are the evidence boundary. Local drafts, generated queues and historical notes are not proof that a platform, API, network, account flow, transfer rail or policy state is current.

### What should be checked before acting?

Check the official URL, product type, jurisdiction or account scope, recovery route, network or settlement rail, support path, rate limit or transfer status, and whether any action exposes credentials, recovery phrases, private keys, API secrets, personal identity documents or balances.

### What should remain unpublished?

Do not publish secret material, credential fields, identity documents, support ticket private data, personal balances, seed phrases, hidden affiliate promises, unverified rewards, price predictions, fake licensing claims, fake traffic claims or indexing claims.

## Practical Takeaway

The safest version of this article is the one that stays boring and exact. A safe Gate US onboarding path should finish identity and security controls before any first meaningful withdrawal. Gate US registration guidance says users create an account with email or phone and confirm a 6-digit code. Gate US identity-verification guidance says users must pass KYC to access trading services including deposit, withdrawal and transfer, with review typically ranging from half an hour to 12 hours. Gate US fund-password guidance says the fund password is set in Security and must differ from the login password. Gate US authenticator guidance says an authenticator is required for login, withdrawals, password changes and other security operations. Gate US withdrawal-whitelist guidance says a verification-free trusted address can skip later withdrawal verification, so the safer tutorial is to verify identity, bind authenticator, set fund password, add only a controlled address, and stop if any helper asks for codes, passwords, seed phrases or private keys. The user outcome is a clearer next inspection step, not a promise that a platform, API, transfer route or tokenized asset will work under every future condition.

## Verified Fact Boundary

This article is intentionally narrow. It does not rank products by price, predict token performance, claim regulatory approval beyond the cited wording, or tell the reader that any exchange, API, wallet, stablecoin rail, tokenized-asset route or compliance framework is universally safe. It maps what the cited official or institutional sources say into a decision checklist.

1. SEC Crypto@SEC lists a September 25, 2026 FAQ related to federal securities laws for certain crypto assets and transactions.
2. SEC Crypto@SEC ties that FAQ to the Commission's March 17, 2026 Interpretive Release.
3. SEC Crypto@SEC lists September 17, 2026 temporary conditional exemptive relief for tokenized NMS stock trading venues.
4. SEC Crypto@SEC lists a September 1, 2026 transfer-agent proposal addressing electronic and blockchain-based recordkeeping.
5. The SEC items are different source types and should not be collapsed into blanket approval claims.

## Decision Matrix

| Check | What it means | Practical action | Unknown to keep explicit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source type | FAQ, interpretive release, exemption and proposal have different legal functions | label the source type before quoting | future court or Commission action |
| Date | Crypto@SEC lists multiple September 2026 items | record the exact SEC date and URL | later updates |
| Scope | crypto-asset FAQs do not automatically govern tokenized NMS stock venue relief | match topic to source category | edge-case products |
| Rule status | a proposal is not a final rule | separate proposed obligations from current conditions | comment-period changes |
| Stop rule | SEC material does not create an investment recommendation | stop if an article turns source classification into approval language | private compliance posture |

## Source Map

- SEC: [Crypto@SEC](https://www.sec.gov/securities-topics/crypto-task-force/cryptosec) (sec-crypto)
- SEC: [FAQs - Application of the Federal Securities Laws to Certain Types of Crypto Assets and Certain Transactions Involving Crypto Assets](https://www.sec.gov/securities-topics/crypto-task-force/crypto-asset-faqs) (sec-faq-crypto-assets)
- SEC: [Interpretive Release on Certain Types of Crypto Assets and Certain Transactions Involving Crypto Assets](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/2026/03/33-11350) (sec-interpretive-release)
- SEC: [Fact Sheet: Conditional Exemptive Relief for Tokenized NMS Stock](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/other/2026/34-106444-fact-sheet.pdf) (sec-tokenized-nms-fact-sheet)

The source map separates first-party operational documentation from institutional analysis. A venue help page can prove what the venue says about account opening, API behavior, transfer status, whitelists, withdrawal controls or supported routes. An institutional source can prove a policy frame or market-structure concern. Neither type proves a user's private account state, a future fee, a future recovery outcome, a future approval, or a guarantee that support will resolve an error.

## How to Use This Checklist

Start with the exact product type. A brokerage stock order, a WebSocket connection, a withdrawal whitelist, a tokenized-fund shareclass, a reimbursement program, a security hold and an account-opening flow are different operational objects. If the source uses familiar words such as account, address, order, transfer, approval, finality, verification, coverage or support, still check the mechanism underneath. The mechanism decides who can act, who can reverse or review a problem, what evidence is required, and what remains outside the user's control.

Second, verify the route. A reader should name the exact official page, exact product surface, exact chain or network, exact account or wallet type and exact action under review. If the evidence cannot be tied to those specifics, the content remains educational context rather than a publishable operational claim. This protects the article from overreaching: it is better to say unknown than to turn a help-page sentence into a guarantee.

Third, separate convenience from obligation. A smoother interface, faster transfer, lower apparent friction, more familiar brand or more complete policy framework does not create legal rights by itself. Recovery, whitelisting, reimbursement, redemption, finality, account approval, order execution, API availability and regulatory supervision depend on documented obligations and current product controls. A reader should be able to take the checklist and decide what to inspect next without being pushed into an account, deposit, transfer, trade or integration.

## Control Notes

### 1. Source type

Source type is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means FAQ, interpretive release, exemption and proposal have different legal functions. The useful action is to label the source type before quoting. The unresolved edge is future court or Commission action, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, source type should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material. The record can stay simple: the official source URL, the date checked, the product or network under review, and a non-secret note describing why the next step is acceptable. Screenshots should avoid balances, identity documents, API keys, recovery phrases, private keys, passphrases, verification codes and support-ticket private data.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative. If the public source changes later, the right response is to update the article with a new date and source map. The wrong response is to defend an old queue, old screenshot, social repost, search snippet, AI summary or generated draft as current proof. This is the rule that makes the content useful for answer engines and safe enough for a reader: the conclusion can be quoted without stripping away the condition attached to it.

### 2. Date

The useful action is to record the exact SEC date and URL. The unresolved edge is later updates, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, date should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 3. Scope

In this package, it means crypto-asset FAQs do not automatically govern tokenized NMS stock venue relief. The useful action is to match topic to source category. The unresolved edge is edge-case products, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, scope should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

### 4. Rule status

Rule status is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means a proposal is not a final rule. The useful action is to separate proposed obligations from current conditions. The unresolved edge is comment-period changes, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, rule status should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 5. Stop rule

Stop rule is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means SEC material does not create an investment recommendation. The useful action is to stop if an article turns source classification into approval language. The unresolved edge is private compliance posture, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, stop rule should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

## Known Unknowns

- future court or Commission action
- later updates
- edge-case products
- comment-period changes
- private compliance posture

These unknowns are not filler. They are the part of the article that prevents a source-backed guide from becoming an unsafe recommendation. If a future source resolves one of them, the correct action is to update the article with a new source and date, not to backfill certainty into this version.

## FAQ

### Is this article investment advice?

No. It is a source-mapped operational and decision checklist. It does not recommend buying, selling, staking, depositing, withdrawing, migrating, holding, borrowing against or tokenizing any asset.

### Can a reader rely on an old screenshot or local draft?

No. The cited source URLs and the review date are the evidence boundary. Local drafts, generated queues and historical notes are not proof that a platform, API, network, account flow, transfer rail or policy state is current.

### What should be checked before acting?

Check the official URL, product type, jurisdiction or account scope, recovery route, network or settlement rail, support path, rate limit or transfer status, and whether any action exposes credentials, recovery phrases, private keys, API secrets, personal identity documents or balances.

### What should remain unpublished?

Do not publish secret material, credential fields, identity documents, support ticket private data, personal balances, seed phrases, hidden affiliate promises, unverified rewards, price predictions, fake licensing claims, fake traffic claims or indexing claims.

## Practical Takeaway

The safest version of this article is the one that stays boring and exact. The SEC Crypto@SEC page turns late-September crypto guidance into a source-routing problem for product and venue articles. SEC Crypto@SEC lists a September 25, 2026 FAQ on applying federal securities laws to certain crypto assets and transactions, tied to the Commission's March 17, 2026 Interpretive Release. The same page also lists September 17, 2026 temporary conditional exemptive relief for tokenized NMS stock venues and a September 1, 2026 transfer-agent modernization proposal touching electronic and blockchain-based recordkeeping. A useful action map does not merge those items into one approval story. It separates interpretive guidance, exemptive relief, proposed rulemaking and staff or divisional views before using SEC material in any exchange, tokenized-stock, RWA or custody article. The user outcome is a clearer next inspection step, not a promise that a platform, API, transfer route or tokenized asset will work under every future condition.

content.en:
## Verified Fact Boundary

This article is intentionally narrow. It does not rank products by price, predict token performance, claim regulatory approval beyond the cited wording, or tell the reader that any exchange, API, wallet, stablecoin rail, tokenized-asset route or compliance framework is universally safe. It maps what the cited official or institutional sources say into a decision checklist.

1. Binance says Travel Rule implementation can require users to provide originator or beneficiary information during crypto deposits and withdrawals.
2. Binance says self-hosted wallet verification can involve a Satoshi Test, a small transfer used to prove address control.
3. Binance says Travel Rule address-book information can help pre-validate stored addresses for future transfers.
4. Binance's deposit and withdrawal support hub separates crypto deposit, crypto withdrawal and Travel Parameters guidance.
5. Binance's Travel Rule procedure material describes pop-up information requests for sender or beneficiary details in affected transfer flows.

## Decision Matrix

| Check | What it means | Practical action | Unknown to keep explicit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jurisdiction scope | where Travel Rule questions apply | check whether the user's region and counterparty route are in scope | future jurisdiction expansion |
| Counterparty type | exchange, VASP, self-hosted wallet or third party | classify the beneficiary before submitting details | hidden intermediary review |
| Address control | whether the user controls a self-hosted address | complete only official verification steps | failed or expired Satoshi Test |
| Address-book data | stored recipient and wallet information | keep address-book records current and non-secret | future recipient changes |
| Deposit information | originator information requested for incoming transfers | obtain accurate sender information before deposit follow-up | sender cooperation |
| Withdrawal information | beneficiary information requested for outgoing transfers | confirm name, address and relationship before withdrawal | additional review |
| Privacy boundary | what personal data is shared for compliance | read Binance privacy and transfer wording before acting | counterparty data handling |
| Delay handling | what to do if information is incomplete | pause instead of retrying blindly | support response timing |
| Evidence packet | official URL, checked date, route type and non-secret status | do not publish wallet addresses, names, IDs or codes | private account decision |
| Stop rule | when a transfer claim should not publish | stop if jurisdiction, counterparty, address control or data requirement is unclear | future Binance policy changes |

## Source Map

- Binance Support: [What Is the Travel Rule?](https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/043dabde69ed432295329652094b4a34) (binance-travel-rule)
- Binance Support: [What Is Satoshi Test and Travel Rule Address Book Feature?](https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/0144ac061746409fae64a2166a214fa4) (binance-satoshi-address-book)
- Binance Support: [Crypto Deposit/Withdrawal FAQ](https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/list/310) (binance-deposit-withdrawal-hub)
- Binance Support: [Travel Rule: Crypto Transfer Procedures](https://www.binance.com/en-IN/support/announcement/detail/bd913751319e4e72aae1365b992ea884) (binance-travel-rule-procedure)

The source map separates first-party operational documentation from institutional analysis. A venue help page can prove what the venue says about account opening, API behavior, transfer status, whitelists, withdrawal controls or supported routes. An institutional source can prove a policy frame or market-structure concern. Neither type proves a user's private account state, a future fee, a future recovery outcome, a future approval, or a guarantee that support will resolve an error.

## How to Use This Checklist

Start with the exact product type. A brokerage stock order, a WebSocket connection, a withdrawal whitelist, a tokenized-fund shareclass, a reimbursement program, a security hold and an account-opening flow are different operational objects. If the source uses familiar words such as account, address, order, transfer, approval, finality, verification, coverage or support, still check the mechanism underneath. The mechanism decides who can act, who can reverse or review a problem, what evidence is required, and what remains outside the user's control.

Second, verify the route. A reader should name the exact official page, exact product surface, exact chain or network, exact account or wallet type and exact action under review. If the evidence cannot be tied to those specifics, the content remains educational context rather than a publishable operational claim. This protects the article from overreaching: it is better to say unknown than to turn a help-page sentence into a guarantee.

Third, separate convenience from obligation. A smoother interface, faster transfer, lower apparent friction, more familiar brand or more complete policy framework does not create legal rights by itself. Recovery, whitelisting, reimbursement, redemption, finality, account approval, order execution, API availability and regulatory supervision depend on documented obligations and current product controls. A reader should be able to take the checklist and decide what to inspect next without being pushed into an account, deposit, transfer, trade or integration.

## Control Notes

### 1. Jurisdiction scope

Jurisdiction scope is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means where Travel Rule questions apply. The useful action is to check whether the user's region and counterparty route are in scope. The unresolved edge is future jurisdiction expansion, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, jurisdiction scope should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material. The record can stay simple: the official source URL, the date checked, the product or network under review, and a non-secret note describing why the next step is acceptable. Screenshots should avoid balances, identity documents, API keys, recovery phrases, private keys, passphrases, verification codes and support-ticket private data.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative. If the public source changes later, the right response is to update the article with a new date and source map. The wrong response is to defend an old queue, old screenshot, social repost, search snippet, AI summary or generated draft as current proof. This is the rule that makes the content useful for answer engines and safe enough for a reader: the conclusion can be quoted without stripping away the condition attached to it.

### 2. Counterparty type

Counterparty type is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means exchange, VASP, self-hosted wallet or third party. The useful action is to classify the beneficiary before submitting details. The unresolved edge is hidden intermediary review, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, counterparty type should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

### 3. Address control

The unresolved edge is future recipient changes, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, address-book data should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

### 5. Deposit information

Deposit information is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means originator information requested for incoming transfers. The useful action is to obtain accurate sender information before deposit follow-up. The unresolved edge is sender cooperation, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

### 6. Withdrawal information

Withdrawal information is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means beneficiary information requested for outgoing transfers. The useful action is to confirm name, address and relationship before withdrawal. The unresolved edge is additional review, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, withdrawal information should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 7. Privacy boundary

Privacy boundary is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means what personal data is shared for compliance. The useful action is to read Binance privacy and transfer wording before acting. The unresolved edge is counterparty data handling, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, privacy boundary should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 8. Delay handling

Delay handling is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means what to do if information is incomplete. The useful action is to pause instead of retrying blindly. The unresolved edge is support response timing, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, delay handling should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 9. Evidence packet

Evidence packet is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means official URL, checked date, route type and non-secret status. The useful action is to do not publish wallet addresses, names, IDs or codes. The unresolved edge is private account decision, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, evidence packet should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

### 10. Stop rule

Stop rule is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means when a transfer claim should not publish. The useful action is to stop if jurisdiction, counterparty, address control or data requirement is unclear. The unresolved edge is future Binance policy changes, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, stop rule should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative.

## Known Unknowns

- future jurisdiction expansion
- hidden intermediary review
- failed or expired Satoshi Test
- future recipient changes
- sender cooperation
- additional review
- counterparty data handling
- support response timing
- private account decision
- future Binance policy changes

These unknowns are not filler. They are the part of the article that prevents a source-backed guide from becoming an unsafe recommendation. If a future source resolves one of them, the correct action is to update the article with a new source and date, not to backfill certainty into this version.

## FAQ

### Is this article investment advice?

No. It is a source-mapped operational and decision checklist. It does not recommend buying, selling, staking, depositing, withdrawing, migrating, holding, borrowing against or tokenizing any asset.

### Can a reader rely on an old screenshot or local draft?

No. The cited source URLs and the review date are the evidence boundary. Local drafts, generated queues and historical notes are not proof that a platform, API, network, account flow, transfer rail or policy state is current.

### What should be checked before acting?

Check the official URL, product type, jurisdiction or account scope, recovery route, network or settlement rail, support path, rate limit or transfer status, and whether any action exposes credentials, recovery phrases, private keys, API secrets, personal identity documents or balances.

### What should remain unpublished?

Do not publish secret material, credential fields, identity documents, support ticket private data, personal balances, seed phrases, hidden affiliate promises, unverified rewards, price predictions, fake licensing claims, fake traffic claims or indexing claims.

## Practical Takeaway

The safest version of this article is the one that stays boring and exact. Binance's Travel Rule material turns crypto deposits and withdrawals into an information-quality workflow, not just a wallet-address workflow. Binance says users may need to provide originator or beneficiary information for transfers in jurisdictions where Travel Rule rules apply. Its Satoshi Test and Travel Rule Address Book FAQ says a self-hosted wallet can require a small verification transaction and that stored Travel Rule address information can pre-validate future transfers. The practical decision is to verify the jurisdiction, beneficiary type, address ownership, stored address details and privacy boundary before assuming a withdrawal or deposit will process normally. The user outcome is a clearer next inspection step, not a promise that a platform, API, transfer route or tokenized asset will work under every future condition.

## 常见问题

### 这篇文章是投资建议吗？

不是。本文是来源映射和操作核验清单，不建议买入、卖出、质押、存入、提现、迁移、持有、借贷、集成 API 或代币化任何资产。

### 可以依赖旧截图或本地草稿吗？

不可以。证据边界是本文列出的官方 URL 与核验日期。本地队列、生成草稿、历史记录或旧截图，都不能证明当前平台、网络、账户流程、转账轨道或政策状态。

### 行动前最少应核验什么？

至少核验官方域名、产品类型、地区或账户范围、恢复路径、网络或结算轨道、支持路径、费率和限制，以及是否会暴露凭据、恢复短语、私钥、API secret、个人证件或余额信息。

### 哪些内容不能发布？

不能发布秘密材料、验证码、身份文件、支持单私密内容、个人余额、seed phrase、隐藏返佣承诺、未核验奖励、价格预测、虚假牌照、虚假流量或虚假收录声明。

## 实用结论

本文最有价值的地方是克制。Binance 的 Travel Rule 材料把加密入金和提现变成信息质量流程，而不只是钱包地址流程。Binance 表示，在实施 Travel Rule 的司法辖区，用户可能需要提供 originator 或 beneficiary 信息。其 Satoshi Test 与 Travel Rule Address Book FAQ 说明，自托管钱包可能需要通过小额验证交易证明控制权，已保存的 Travel Rule 地址信息可用于预验证后续转账。实际决策是先核验地区、受益人类型、地址控制权、地址簿信息和隐私边界，再判断入金或提现是否可按普通流程处理。 用户应获得一个更清楚的核验路径，而不是一个看似肯定、实则无法由公开证据承担的承诺。

content.en:
## Verified Fact Boundary

This article is intentionally narrow. It does not rank products by price, predict token performance, claim regulatory approval beyond the cited wording, or tell the reader that any exchange, API, wallet, stablecoin rail, tokenized-asset route or compliance framework is universally safe. It maps what the cited official or institutional sources say into a decision checklist.

1. OKX Status describes itself as a hub for system information, maintenance information, issue descriptions and deposit/withdrawal status.
2. Kraken Status is the public status page for Kraken Digital Asset Exchange and lists component status and incidents.
3. Kraken publishes API documentation for programmatic access to status page elements.
4. Coinbase publishes a consumer status page with incidents and component information.
5. Coinbase Exchange publishes a separate status page for Coinbase Exchange services.

## Decision Matrix

| Check | What it means | Practical action | Unknown to keep explicit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Affected service | which product or component is degraded | match the status item to the user's action | unlisted dependency |
| Affected asset | which token, chain or funding rail is named | avoid assuming all assets are affected | asset-specific recovery |
| Incident state | investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved or maintenance | wait for the correct state before retrying | state lag |
| Timestamp | when the update was posted and in which timezone | record the latest timestamp | late updates |
| Maintenance window | scheduled start and completion scope | avoid trading or transfer actions inside window | overrun risk |
| Component scope | web, app, API, WebSocket, custody or funding | separate UI outage from API or funding outage | shared infrastructure |
| Retry rule | when a user should retry an action | retry only after relevant component recovery | private account restrictions |
| API evidence | machine-readable status data | use API only as supporting evidence | API caching |
| Evidence packet | official URL, checked date, service, asset and state | do not publish account screenshots or balances | privacy retention |
| Stop rule | when radar should remain unknown | stop if the page does not name service, asset, state or time | future page redesign |

## Source Map

- OKX: [OKX Status](https://www.okx.com/en-us/status) (okx-status)
- Kraken: [Kraken Status](https://status.kraken.com/) (kraken-status)
- Kraken: [Kraken Status API](https://status.kraken.com/api) (kraken-status-api)
- Coinbase: [Coinbase Status](https://status.coinbase.com/) (coinbase-status)
- Coinbase: [Coinbase Exchange Status](https://status.exchange.coinbase.com/) (coinbase-exchange-status)

The source map separates first-party operational documentation from institutional analysis. A venue help page can prove what the venue says about account opening, API behavior, transfer status, whitelists, withdrawal controls or supported routes. An institutional source can prove a policy frame or market-structure concern. Neither type proves a user's private account state, a future fee, a future recovery outcome, a future approval, or a guarantee that support will resolve an error.

## How to Use This Checklist

Start with the exact product type. A brokerage stock order, a WebSocket connection, a withdrawal whitelist, a tokenized-fund shareclass, a reimbursement program, a security hold and an account-opening flow are different operational objects. If the source uses familiar words such as account, address, order, transfer, approval, finality, verification, coverage or support, still check the mechanism underneath. The mechanism decides who can act, who can reverse or review a problem, what evidence is required, and what remains outside the user's control.

Second, verify the route. A reader should name the exact official page, exact product surface, exact chain or network, exact account or wallet type and exact action under review. If the evidence cannot be tied to those specifics, the content remains educational context rather than a publishable operational claim. This protects the article from overreaching: it is better to say unknown than to turn a help-page sentence into a guarantee.

Third, separate convenience from obligation. A smoother interface, faster transfer, lower apparent friction, more familiar brand or more complete policy framework does not create legal rights by itself. Recovery, whitelisting, reimbursement, redemption, finality, account approval, order execution, API availability and regulatory supervision depend on documented obligations and current product controls. A reader should be able to take the checklist and decide what to inspect next without being pushed into an account, deposit, transfer, trade or integration.

## Control Notes

### 1. Affected service

Affected service is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means which product or component is degraded. The useful action is to match the status item to the user's action. The unresolved edge is unlisted dependency, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

content.en:
## Verified Fact Boundary

This article is intentionally narrow. It does not rank products by price, predict token performance, claim regulatory approval beyond the cited wording, or tell the reader that any exchange, API, wallet, stablecoin rail, tokenized-asset route or compliance framework is universally safe. It maps what the cited official or institutional sources say into a decision checklist.

1. Franklin's Benji page describes tokenizing a traditional money market fund for mutual fund record keeping.
2. Franklin's Benji page says one share of FOBXX equals one BENJI token.
3. Franklin prospectus material says the transfer agent maintains the official record of share ownership through a blockchain-integrated system.
4. Franklin prospectus material connects book-entry recordkeeping features with one or more public blockchain networks.
5. SEC tokenized-securities material says tokenization requires analysis of the associated rights, obligations and benefits, not only the token format.

## Decision Matrix

| Check | What it means | Practical action | Unknown to keep explicit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Official record | which system is the authoritative ownership record | separate transfer-agent records from token display | record reconciliation timing |
| Fund share | the mutual fund share represented by the token | read fund documents before equating token and cash | share-class updates |
| Transfer agent | the entity maintaining ownership records | identify the responsible recordkeeper | service-provider changes |
| Blockchain role | public networks used for transaction activity or record integration | distinguish network record from legal entitlement | network eligibility |
| Wallet eligibility | which wallets or networks may be used | verify eligibility before transfer | private eligibility decision |
| Redemption and liquidity | how fund shares can be redeemed or transferred | read prospectus terms before liquidity claims | gates or timing |
| Investor status | who may hold or access the product | verify onboarding and investor requirements | jurisdictional limitations |
| Disclosure source | official fund documents versus marketing descriptions | prefer prospectus and filings for rights claims | future supplement updates |
| Evidence packet | official URL, date, fund, network and record-source note | do not publish wallet IDs or account documents | privacy retention |
| Stop rule | when RWA interpretation should pause | stop if official record, eligibility or redemption route is unclear | future SEC or fund changes |

## Source Map

- Franklin Templeton Digital Assets: [Invest with Benji](https://digitalassets.franklintempleton.com/benji/?hsLang=en) (franklin-benji)
- Franklin Templeton: [Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund Prospectus](https://www.franklintempleton.com/forms-literature/download-preview/9001-P) (franklin-prospectus)
- SEC EDGAR: [Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1786958/000165558926000970/c485bpos.htm) (sec-edgar-fobxx)
- SEC: [Statement on Tokenized Securities](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/corp-fin-statement-tokenized-securities-012826-statement-tokenized-securities) (sec-tokenized-securities)

The source map separates first-party operational documentation from institutional analysis. A venue help page can prove what the venue says about account opening, API behavior, transfer status, whitelists, withdrawal controls or supported routes. An institutional source can prove a policy frame or market-structure concern. Neither type proves a user's private account state, a future fee, a future recovery outcome, a future approval, or a guarantee that support will resolve an error.

## How to Use This Checklist

Start with the exact product type. A brokerage stock order, a WebSocket connection, a withdrawal whitelist, a tokenized-fund shareclass, a reimbursement program, a security hold and an account-opening flow are different operational objects. If the source uses familiar words such as account, address, order, transfer, approval, finality, verification, coverage or support, still check the mechanism underneath. The mechanism decides who can act, who can reverse or review a problem, what evidence is required, and what remains outside the user's control.

Second, verify the route. A reader should name the exact official page, exact product surface, exact chain or network, exact account or wallet type and exact action under review. If the evidence cannot be tied to those specifics, the content remains educational context rather than a publishable operational claim. This protects the article from overreaching: it is better to say unknown than to turn a help-page sentence into a guarantee.

Third, separate convenience from obligation. A smoother interface, faster transfer, lower apparent friction, more familiar brand or more complete policy framework does not create legal rights by itself. Recovery, whitelisting, reimbursement, redemption, finality, account approval, order execution, API availability and regulatory supervision depend on documented obligations and current product controls. A reader should be able to take the checklist and decide what to inspect next without being pushed into an account, deposit, transfer, trade or integration.

## Control Notes

### 1. Official record

Official record is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means which system is the authoritative ownership record. The useful action is to separate transfer-agent records from token display. The unresolved edge is record reconciliation timing, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, official record should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material. The record can stay simple: the official source URL, the date checked, the product or network under review, and a non-secret note describing why the next step is acceptable. Screenshots should avoid balances, identity documents, API keys, recovery phrases, private keys, passphrases, verification codes and support-ticket private data.

The evidence standard is deliberately conservative. If the public source changes later, the right response is to update the article with a new date and source map. The wrong response is to defend an old queue, old screenshot, social repost, search snippet, AI summary or generated draft as current proof. This is the rule that makes the content useful for answer engines and safe enough for a reader: the conclusion can be quoted without stripping away the condition attached to it.

### 2. Fund share

Fund share is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means the mutual fund share represented by the token. The useful action is to read fund documents before equating token and cash. The unresolved edge is share-class updates, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, fund share should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

For an operator, blockchain role should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.

### 5. Wallet eligibility

Wallet eligibility is the part of the decision where the reader must turn a public source into an operating rule. In this package, it means which wallets or networks may be used. The useful action is to verify eligibility before transfer. The unresolved edge is private eligibility decision, so this article does not convert that uncertainty into a promise, ranking, reward, approval, safety claim or future-availability claim.

For an operator, wallet eligibility should be recorded before funds, account access, wallet recovery, API order flow, whitelist changes, cross-chain transfers or tokenized-asset decisions become material.
